name: guardrails
description: The authority layer under the other technical-delivery plugins: what the agent may do on its own, and what it must show the user first. Defines 56 rules across seven ID'd families — consent (nothing gets built without an explicit go-ahead, implementation included and not just commands or database writes; no assumptions, so any detail the user hasn't pinned down and the repo's docs don't answer becomes a question rather than a quiet default; batched multiple-choice questions; never let a default pass silently; and a proportionality rule so the form of the stop scales to the change — a one-property, already-diagnosed fix gets a one-line ask, not the five-field block), preview-before-permission (show the exact command, its resolved target, a sample from a read-only probe actually run, whether it is reversible, and what a standing 'always allow' grant would authorise for the rest of the session), data and destructive operations (confirm the environment, count affected rows before writing them, migrations show up and down together, production data never moves downward), verification (a failed test is not a verdict — report the real output, label the explanation as a hypothesis, ask before changing code, and stop after two attempts), orchestration (decompose into small-context subtasks with acceptance criteria declared at dispatch, verify each result against them, memoise completed subtasks so a retry reuses finished work, ask before spending another agent, and stage any bulk change — more than about five files pilots on ONE first, shows the real diff, and confirms the pattern before the rest, because a script enlarges the blast radius rather than shrinking the review), scope, and transparency. Rules are tiered Hard/Soft/Guidance; sibling plugins reference them by ID rather than restating them. Ships reference skills for the four families that need worked examples rather than a rule line. Also ships six hooks: a SessionStart contract carrying the four load-bearing rules plus a skill-routing table with explicit tie-breaks for the phrases several skills legitimately claim, a UserPromptSubmit hook that gates every non-trivial request behind a scope block (what I understood / what I'd build / what I'm not doing / what's unpinned / which skill applies) and then stops for a go-ahead rather than proceeding — one stop at the start of a piece of work, never a stop per file — while staying silent on acknowledgements and definitional questions, a PreToolUse Bash/PowerShell gate that blocks destructive and database-write commands until a preview has actually been shown to the user (verified via transcript evidence that a real user turn intervened — the one signal a model cannot fabricate, with harness-injected isMeta entries excluded) and blocks git commit, push, merge, rebase and PR creation outright with no preview path (the agent drafts commit messages and PR descriptions as text, with no Claude/AI attribution), a PreToolUse Edit/Write gate that hard-gates only database work — migrations, SQL, ORM models, seeds, connection config, or any file whose new content writes raw SQL — until a scope block has been shown and the user has answered it, leaving ordinary code edits unblocked, a PreToolUse Agent gate that refuses a sub-agent dispatch declaring no acceptance criteria, and a PostToolUse Bash injector that delivers the failure-triage contract when a test or build run fails, escalating after the third attempt on the same command. All three fail open on every uncertainty, and read-only probes are never blocked — otherwise the model could not produce the preview it is being ordered to produce. Escape hatches at three tiers: KZ_GUARDRAILS=off for CI and headless runs, and a per-project ~/.claude/kaizen/<project-key>/guardrails.json with allow_patterns for a team's own safe wrapper scripts. Ships a self-test (scripts/selftest.js, 174 checks) because the transcript-format dependency is the one failure that would otherwise be silent.
